purpose: Official Razorpay and RazorpayX context used to supplement Supabase RAG when retrieval is sparse. It must not override newer approved Supabase records or invent commercials.

products.name: Smart Collect 2.0
products.merchant_problem: The business receives direct bank-transfer or UPI collections from many customers and struggles to identify, match or reconcile each incoming payment.
fit: Creates Customer Identifiers on demand for receiving NEFT, RTGS and IMPS payments.
Smart Collect 2.0 extends collection to UPI through Virtual UPI IDs / VPAs.
Automatically reconciles incoming payments against identifiers and provides account-level visibility.
Supports real-time payment notifications through webhooks.
Can support many-customers-to-one-account and many-customers-to-many-accounts collection models.
Third-Party Validation is available for supported Smart Collect flows subject to prerequisites.
qualify: How do customers pay you today: UPI, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, payment links, cards, or a mix?
Is the main problem accepting the payment, or identifying which customer/invoice an incoming transfer belongs to?
Do you want one identifier per customer, order, invoice or business account?
Roughly how many incoming transfers do you reconcile in a month?
Do you need payer validation or restrictions on which bank accounts can pay?

products.name: RazorpayX Payouts
products.merchant_problem: The business needs to send money out to vendors, suppliers, contractors, customers or other beneficiaries reliably and at scale.
fit: Payouts are transactions to contacts and their fund accounts.
Payouts can be created and processed from the RazorpayX Dashboard and through supported APIs.
Supported payout modes include IMPS, NEFT, RTGS and UPI, subject to product/account rules and limits.
Businesses can use payout purposes, attachments, summaries, bulk workflows and payout status tracking.
New merchants should be guided through the currently supported RazorpayX account route and KYC before live payouts.
qualify: Who are you paying: vendors, suppliers, contractors, employees, customers or another group?
Roughly how many payouts do you make per day or month?
Do you want to trigger payouts manually, upload them in bulk, or automate them through APIs?
Which payout modes matter to you: bank transfer, UPI, or both?
What is painful today: approvals, beneficiary creation, reconciliation, status tracking, failed payouts, or manual execution?

products.name: RazorpayX Current Account
products.merchant_problem: The business wants a banking account layer for day-to-day business money movement and RazorpayX workflows.
fit: RazorpayX provides business banking capabilities including Current Account and Payouts workflows.
Account opening, KYC, serviceability and banking-partner approval must be confirmed before activation.
Do not infer a commercial, minimum balance or approval SLA unless the latest approved record is retrieved.
qualify: What is the legal entity type and what does the business do?
Is the account mainly for day-to-day banking, payouts, collections, or a combination?
What is the approximate monthly transaction volume?
Do you already have a business current account and, if yes, what is missing from the current setup?

products.name: RazorpayX Escrow
products.merchant_problem: A platform or marketplace needs customer funds to be held or controlled before release to sellers, service providers or another beneficiary group.
fit: Escrow should be explored when the business model genuinely requires controlled holding and release of funds.
Final structure, serviceability, trustee/bank requirements and commercials require specialist review and approved records.
Do not confuse ordinary vendor payouts with escrow merely because a merchant has many vendors.
qualify: Why do funds need to be held before release, and who ultimately receives them?
Is the marketplace/platform already live?
How are customer payments collected today?
What event or condition should trigger release to the seller or service provider?
Do you have the relevant merchant/vendor agreements and transaction evidence for review?

products.name: Razorpay Payment Gateway
products.merchant_problem: The business needs customers to pay online through a website, app or digital checkout flow.
fit: Payment Gateway is the primary route for online customer payment acceptance across supported payment modes.
If the real problem is reconciliation of direct bank transfers rather than checkout, evaluate Smart Collect 2.0 instead of defaulting to Payment Gateway.
If the merchant is a marketplace that must split payments among parties, evaluate the relevant marketplace routing/split-payment product separately.
qualify: Where will customers pay you: website, mobile app, invoices, links, or direct bank transfer?
Are payments one-time, recurring, or both?
What payment modes and monthly volume matter most?
Is checkout conversion the problem, or is reconciliation/settlement the bigger pain point?

conversation_rules: The merchant should never need to know Razorpay product names. Start from the business problem and infer the likely product family.
Ask one or two high-value questions at a time rather than presenting a form-like checklist.
When two needs are present, preserve both and qualify them separately.
Do not recommend Smart Collect 2.0 merely because a merchant says UPI. Recommend it when the problem involves direct-transfer collection and reconciliation or unique customer identifiers.
Do not recommend Payouts merely because a merchant mentions vendors; first confirm these are outgoing business payments and understand scale/automation needs.
Do not recommend Escrow merely because a merchant is a marketplace; confirm that funds actually need controlled holding/release.
Never invent pricing, serviceability, activation timelines, links or approval conditions.
